diagnosis.root_cause: Two active CRM records with different ONU MAC addresses are assigned to the same physical slot EPON0/4:17. Only one ONU can occupy that slot, indicating a duplicate or stale ONU provisioning record.
evidence: The target ONU is currently online and responding, with Auth/Finish state, so it is not currently offline.
RX power is -20.91 dBm and TX power is 2.38 dBm, both within the calibrated normal ranges.
Seven days of RX, TX, bias current, distance, voltage, and temperature telemetry are stable; there is no fibre degradation, laser degradation, or distance change.
The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and subtree queries, with healthy CPU, memory, and temperature; the router heartbeat is also healthy.
All probed surviving ONUs on EPON0/4 are online, and the customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1044.
Session count is normal at 2 in 24 hours with approximately normal session durations, so there is no session-flapping diagnosis.

The explicit duplicate-slot conflict identifies two active CRM records, with different ONU MACs, both assigned to EPON0/4:17. This is the direct fault evidence and affects the two customer records sharing the slot.

remediation.action: Inspect the two records for slot EPON0/4:17, identify the valid subscriber and physical ONU, remove or correct the stale duplicate CRM/OLT entry, and assign the displaced ONU a unique slot. Reconcile the ONU MAC, line ID, CRM record, and OLT registration, then verify both customers authenticate and remain online.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two active CRM records place different ONU MACs on EPON0/4:17. A slot holds exactly one ONU, so one record is stale. The live probe returns a single device, and its MAC matches the subject record, identifying the other as the leftover.
expected_reasoning: The CRM view lists two active customers on EPON0/4:17 with different ONU MACs
A PON slot holds exactly one ONU, so this state is physically impossible
The live probe of that slot returns a single responding device
The probe's optical values match the subject record's cached reading of -20.88 dBm
RADIUS holds a consistent entry for the subject with normal sessions and traffic
The second record therefore does not correspond to an installed device and is stale
The optical layer is healthy and neither customer is experiencing a service fault
This is a record defect of the same class as the 644 such interfaces in the estate

expected_escalation.review_reason: One of two CRM records on this slot is stale; deleting the wrong one disconnects a live customer

distractors: Nothing is failing and no customer has complained
Both records are marked active and look equally legitimate in CRM
